newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM, unions agree on 17 pct pay rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM, unions agree on 17 pct pay rise.

text.p: The board and trade unions at Poland's KGHM copper concern agreed on Wednesday that average wages in the company would rise 17 percent this year instead of 15 percent, a union leader said on Wednesday.

Krzysztof Baczek, head of the Solidarity's Copper Smelting and Processing union told Reuters the seven unions which went on a strike alert last week would meet on Thursday morning to decide whether to drop the strike readiness.

"The board and unions agreed on the 17 percent wage rise this year instead of the 15 percent, although we did not have the necessary authorisation to agree to the proposed pay-out method proposed by the board," Baczek said.
"All the unions which went on strike alert will meet tomorrow morning in the Rudna mine to decide whether to keep the strike alert or drop it," he said.

The board proposes that the 17 percent average wage increase would be implemented through a 8.5-percent raise on April 1 and another two-percent rise on July 1, following a 6.5 percent rise in January.
The firm has 23,400 workers. Three of the unions involved said they would tell the board on Friday whether they accepted the terms.

The unions also demanded that the board raises the basic wage by 10 percent and give workers of the company, due to be floated on the Warsaw and London bourses later this year, employment and social benefits guarantees.
A source close to the talks told Reuters the board would be willing to discuss the union's remaining demands during their regular quarterly meetings. --Jan Strupczewski +48 22 653 9700
